recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is +15.7% above baseline (72.6 vs 62.8 ms), indicating strong parasympathetic resilience
Resting HR is -6.1% below baseline (48.8 vs 51.9 bpm), supporting recovery adaptation

readiness.guidance: The body is physiologically resilient but functionally fatigued; prioritize sleep consolidation and avoid intensity until readiness scores rise above 45.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp volume drop and pacing regression after a high-volume July, but with improved efficiency and lower aerobic TE — suggesting a deliberate taper or fatigue-driven slowdown rather than deconditioning.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +31 spm this month (149 vs 118 in July), the largest monthly shift in the dataset — and it coincides with markedly slower pace and lower HR, suggesting compensatory form adjustments likely due to fatigue or reduced neuromuscular drive.

goal_tracker.message: Matching last month’s volume would require 72.3 km across 11 sessions (~6.6 km/session) in 24 days — but current readiness (score 25), chronic sleep debt (14/14 nights <7h), and recent aerobic decoupling spikes (7.09%, median 7.11%) make this unsafe and counterproductive; chasing volume now risks injury and undermines long-term aerobic development.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated running economy
insights.body: Despite HRV and resting HR improvements, running economy has worsened (13.89 vs 13.64) while sleep remains at 4.8h/night — and the worst recent economy value (262.2 ml/kg/km) occurred on a day following only 4.2h sleep (not shown in summary but present in raw logs); sleep restriction impairs mitochondrial efficiency and neuromuscular coordination.

insights.title: ACWR stability masks rising aerobic fragility
insights.body: ACWR is optimal (0.9) and recovery balance is positive (+2.48), yet aerobic decoupling is elevated (7.09%, median 7.11%) — well above the 5% aerobic threshold — indicating the cardiovascular system is struggling to sustain efficiency even at moderate loads, likely due to unresolved fatigue from July’s high volume (82.4 km).

insights.title: Cadence–pace dissociation signals neuromuscular fatigue
insights.body: Cadence surged to 149 spm (up from 118 in July) while pace slowed (532 vs 518 sec/km) and HR dropped — an atypical pattern where higher turnover doesn’t yield faster speed, suggesting compromised stride power and reliance on shorter, less efficient steps to maintain rhythm under fatigue.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance persists despite lower volume
insights.body: Zone 3 still accounts for 28% of this month’s work (vs 29% in July and 31% in June), even as total volume collapsed — meaning the runner is spending disproportionate time in the 'gray zone' where training stimulus is suboptimal for endurance or speed development, likely reinforcing aerobic inefficiency.

recommendations.action: Complete two 45-minute Zone 2 runs (HR ≤135 bpm) on Tuesday and Thursday, focusing on relaxed breathing and cadence control at 152–155 spm — no pace target
recommendations.reason: Maintains aerobic stimulus without accumulating fatigue; aligns with current readiness score (25) and elevated decoupling

recommendations.action: Perform one 20-minute barefoot or minimalist-shoe walking session on Saturday, outdoors, at natural pace — no HR monitoring
recommendations.reason: Stimulates foot proprioception and gait retraining without load; addresses cadence–efficiency mismatch and vertical oscillation (7.9 mm, above recent median of 7.7 mm)

recommendations.action: Prioritize sleep hygiene: lights out by 22:00, no screens after 21:00, and aim for ≥6h nightly — track sleep hours daily and pause running if <5.5h for two consecutive nights
recommendations.reason: Sleep is the only severely suppressed recovery metric (14/14 nights <7h) and directly impacts running economy and decoupling

risk_flags.evidence: Aerobic decoupling median = 7.11%, latest = 7.09% — both >5% threshold; VO2max stable (39.8) but efficiency declining (13.89 vs 13.42 in May)
risk_flags.action: Avoid Zone 4+ efforts until decoupling drops below 5% for two consecutive runs

risk_flags.evidence: 14/14 nights <7h sleep; recent avg = 4.8h (baseline = 4.4h), but absolute duration remains pathologically low
risk_flags.action: Implement mandatory sleep window (22:00–05:00) for next 7 days before reassessing readiness

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish gait efficiency and autonomic regulation through low-stress movement and non-negotiable sleep extension — not volume or intensity.
suggested_sessions: Barefoot walk (20 min, outdoor, natural pace)
